| [LIT-021](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-021.md) v3 | From the origin of life to pandemics: emergent phenomena in complex systems | Artime et al. (2022), [ARXIV-2205.11595](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.11595). An editorial review with no new result. Its one formal item (§4, Eq. 4.1: x(t+1) = f[x(t)], x(0) = x₀) sorts phenomena three ways. Non-emergent: local rules plus initial conditions let you deduce the "expected" high-level pattern. Weakly emergent: they let you deduce an "unexpected" one by computation. Strongly emergent: no deduction is possible even in principle. "Unexpected" is never defined. The rest is a cross-domain survey (§3), a 16-paper map of the theme issue (§5), and an outlook (§6). | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 (NOTE-007); worth reading as the table of contents and framing of the Phil. Trans. A theme issue that holds LIT-025 and LIT-027 (§5), and as a quick survey of emergence examples. Do not cite it for a definition of emergence, because its "mathematical" definition leaves the deciding criterion ("unexpected") informal. |
| [LIT-025](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-025.md) v3 | Greater than the parts: a review of the information decomposition approach to causal emergence | Mediano et al. (2022), [ARXIV-2111.06518](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.06518). A review, with no new theorem, of the ΦID theory of causal emergence. A supervenient feature V_t is k-th-order causally emergent iff Un⁽ᵏ⁾(V_t; X_t′ \| X_t) > 0. A system hosts such features iff Syn⁽ᵏ⁾(X_t; X_t′) > 0 (cited as Rosas et al. 2020, Theorem 1), and Syn⁽ᵏ⁾ = D⁽ᵏ⁾ + G⁽ᵏ⁾ (downward causation plus causal decoupling). The review's own additions are interpretive: the formalism is neutral between Granger and Pearl, coordinate dependence is defended as a feature, and it rebuts the charge that the theory makes no macro-versus-micro comparison. | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 (NOTE-010); a short, accurate map of the ΦID emergence formalism and the right entry point to Rosas et al. 2020, which a reader will still need for the proofs, the assumptions and the redundancy-free practical criteria. None of these is stated in the review. |
| [LIT-027](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-027.md) v3 | Emergence as the conversion of information: a unifying theory | Varley et al. (2022), [ARXIV-2104.13368](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.13368). Varley and Hoel apply a PID, with the Williams–Beer I_min redundancy, to past→future mutual information and summarise it with a new layer-weighted "synergy bias" B_syn ∈ [0,1]. Coarse-graining can raise B_syn at the macroscale. A macroscale XOR reaches 0.833, against 0.52 for its NAND/AND/OR implementation. In 200 random 3-node "Gaussian" TPMs expanded into equivalence-class micro/mesoscales with *identical* MI, every macroscale had higher B_syn, by ≈ 0.01–0.07 (r = 0.819 against macroscale B_syn). In 185 near-deterministic systems the change was mostly negative, down to ≈ −0.1. | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 (NOTE-020); a clear, small-scale demonstration that coarse-graining can change the redundant/synergistic composition of information and not just its amount. It is worth reading as the explicit cross-scale counterpoint to the ΦID account (item 21). Its "unifying theory" is a framing: the EI section re-describes a known decomposition and contains no new result. |

| [LIT-045](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-045.md) | Structural Realism | Ladyman (2007), <https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/structural-realism/>. The entry presents structural realism (Worrall 1989) as the attempt to keep both the no-miracles argument and the pessimistic meta-induction: what survives theory change, and what we are entitled to believe, is a theory's mathematical or relational structure. It then separates an epistemic version (we can know only structure) from an ontic version (structure is all there is). The ontic version is motivated by quantum individuality, gauge symmetry and spacetime physics, and faces the "relations without relata" objection. | Deferred — seeded from the abstract and a skim on 2026-09-25; not read in full |
